new_findings_today.title: ROOT CAUSE FOUND for the week-old /api/chat outage: the Anthropic API account has run out of credit balance. Confirmed via first-time Vercel runtime-error-log access — this is a billing issue, not a code bug, and needs a human to add credits.
new_findings_today.detail: Today's run had access to the Vercel MCP's get_runtime_errors tool for the first time in this skill's history. Querying it for /api/chat over the last 7 days returns the exact server-side exception on every failure: Anthropic API HTTP 400, {"type":"invalid_request_error","message":"Your credit balance is too low to access the Anthropic API. Please go to Plans & Billing to upgrade or purchase credits."}. This is not a code regression: (1) the earliest evidence of this exact error is 2026-07-27T02:11:58Z (during last week's QA run) and it is still occurring today at 2026-08-03T02:09:31-46Z — a full week of continuous failure, and (2) chat_logs (the table the route writes a row to on every SUCCESSFUL answer) has zero rows after 2026-07-22T15:31:51Z — meaning the credit exhaustion most likely began somewhere between 2026-07-22 15:31 and the first captured error 2026-07-27 02:11, and NO real visitor has received a working AI chat answer in the 12 days since. Separately, the same Anthropic-credit-exhaustion error is ALSO hitting /api/itinerary (confirmed in the same 7-day error log, 2026-07-28, 07-30, and 08-02) — but /api/itinerary does NOT 500 for users, because its code already catches this specific error and serves a 'deterministic fallback' (log line: 'Anthropic API error — serving deterministic fallback'). /api/chat has no equivalent fallback: its catch-all only special-cases HTTP 429 responses (a difference-in-kind: this Anthropic error is HTTP 400, not 429, so /api/chat's existing 429-branch — which already has a friendlier user-facing message — never fires), and falls through to the generic 500 'Something went wrong'. Directly read apps/web/src/app/api/chat/route.ts today: the hardcoded model='claude-sonnet-4-6' string flagged as a code smell on 07-27 is still unpatched (line 388) but is confirmed NOT the cause — the simple/Haiku path uses a valid model ID (claude-haiku-4-5-20251001) and fails with the identical credit-balance error, and 0 commits to this file have landed since 07-20.

Site-wide 7d error sweep also surfaced 3 matching 'Anthropic API error — serving deterministic fallback' log lines on /api/itinerary (2026-07-28T10:46:19Z, 2026-07-30T11:18:43Z, 2026-08-02T14:40:37Z) with the identical underlying Anthropic error message. chat_logs SELECT ... new_findings_today.recommendation: This needs a human, not a code fix: add credit / upgrade the Anthropic Console billing plan for the account tied to ANTHROPIC_API_KEY (organization id 1624b38e-d736-4dc3-9fe4-6ae72d0962cc, visible in the error response headers). Once credits are restored, chat should recover immediately with no deploy needed — the code path itself is not broken. Two secondary, non-blocking code improvements worth making once the immediate issue is resolved: (1) extend api/chat/route.ts's error handling to also catch this 'credit balance too low' shape (it's a 400, not a 429) and serve the same graceful degraded-mode message /api/itinerary already gives users, so a future billing lapse doesn't take down the whole chat feature with a raw 500; (2) update the hardcoded model='claude-sonnet-4-6' string (line 388) to a current model ID such as claude-sonnet-5 — unrelated to today's root cause but confirmed stale and worth fixing on its own merits. Recommend also setting up an Anthropic Console low-balance alert/auto-reload if available, since this is now a repeat-risk outage class (the flagship differentiating feature going fully dark for a week+ with no automated alerting) rather than a one-off.

new_findings_today.title: Recurring Postgres 'canceling statement due to statement timeout' failures on /explore (both locales), /weekend-from-delhi, and scattered individual destination pages — invisible to this QA harness until today's first-time Vercel error-log access; root cause identified for /explore
new_findings_today.detail: The same 7-day Vercel runtime-error sweep that root-caused the chat outage also surfaced a recurring pattern this harness had never seen before (it previously could only see HTTP status codes, not server-side exception logs): Postgres error 57014 ('canceling statement due to statement timeout') hitting several routes intermittently over the past 7 weeks. Highest-volume: '[explore] destinations fetch failed after retries: canceling statement due to statement timeout' on /en/explore and /hi/explore — 26 occurrences / 7 distinct users between 2026-06-16 and 2026-08-02 (yesterday), plus 12 first-attempt-then-retried instances that recovered without surfacing to the user. Also '[weekend-from:delhi] destinations hydrate failed' on /en/weekend-from-delhi — 10 occurrences / 2 users, 2026-06-18 to 2026-07-30. Also 5 distinct individual destination pages failing with the same 57014 code on getDestination/getMonthData calls, each a handful of times in the 07-28 to 08-01 window: nainital, barmer, bhimbetka, amritsar/november, pfutsero/december. Directly grepped apps/web/src/app/[locale]/explore/page.tsx today: its destinations query does its own inline `createClient(url, key)` and hits `supabase.from("destinations").select(...)` directly on every render — it does NOT go through apps/web/src/lib/cached-data.ts's unstable_cache layer. This is a direct violation of the CLAUDE.md 'Reference-data caching' rule, which was written specifically because uncached `supabase.from("destinations"|...)` reads bypass Next's fetch cache and hit PostgREST fresh on every request — the same class of problem that caused the 2026-06-04 Disk IO/temp-spill alert. The explore-route timeouts start 2026-06-16, twelve days after that incident, and are still recurring as of yesterday. IMPORTANT: /explore is NOT currently broken — it was live-verified working perfectly during today's Section K Chrome pass (200, map rendered with 519 markers, 0 console errors) and Section I (200, 1020ms). This is an intermittent failure under periodic DB load/contention, not a permanent outage — but it is a real, repeated, user-facing failure (7+ real visitors hit a broken /explore page over 7 weeks, most recently yesterday) on one of the site's core navigation surfaces.

Grep of apps/web/src/app/[locale]/explore/page.tsx lines 40-88 shows inline createClient + supabase.from("destinations").select(...) with a manual retry-with-backoff loop (not unstable_cache). Live re-verification today: /en/explore 200 (1020ms, Section I) and fully interactive with 519 Leaflet markers (Section K), 0 console errors.
new_findings_today.recommendation: Route /explore's destinations/states/coords queries through the existing apps/web/src/lib/cached-data.ts cached layer (getCachedDestinationsIndex or equivalent) instead of the current inline per-request createClient + supabase.from(...) call — this is exactly the pattern CLAUDE.md's Reference-data-caching section says to use and explicitly says NOT to bypass. That should both fix the recurring timeouts (fewer, cheaper, cached queries instead of a fresh PostgREST hit + full-catalogue select on every /explore render) and bring this file into compliance with the standing rule. The scattered individual-destination-page timeouts (nainital, barmer, bhimbetka, amritsar, pfutsero) may be a related but distinct DB-load-contention symptom rather than the same root cause — worth a follow-up look at whether they cluster in time with /explore's uncached load spikes, but not conclusively established today. new_findings_today.title: SOS auto-reverify system's first real scheduled weekly run fired on time today; early results show a high 'needs_source' rate that's most likely explained by incomplete source-URL coverage, not a broken verifier
new_findings_today.detail: Migration 072's weekly cron (confirmed via apps/web/vercel.json: schedule "0 0 * * 1", i.e. every Monday 00:00 UTC) fired at 2026-08-03T00:00:27Z — exactly on schedule, and exactly the date the 07-27 QA run predicted as its first real execution (the 07-27T02:18:01Z timestamp visible in the data was a one-off smoke-test shortly after that day's deploy, not the scheduled cron). Status distribution after today's run: 300 rows 'needs_source', 109 'confirmed', 124 'never_run' (409 = 300+109 rows have been touched at least once; the 'bound the run by wall-clock not URL count' fix from 07-27 means each weekly run only gets through part of the 533-row queue before stopping, so 124 untouched rows is expected, not a bug). The 300/409 (73%) 'needs_source' rate looks high in isolation, but source_map (the field that stores a per-number citation URL to check against) is only populated for 159/533 rows total — so a large share of 'needs_source' outcomes are very plausibly rows that simply don't have a source URL registered yet, which is a legitimate, expected status rather than a verification failure. This QA harness cannot fully distinguish 'no source registered' from 'verifier logic bug' without reading the cron's implementation in more depth than today's run budget allowed.
